letter.subject: Concern about cookie and tracking practices on independent.co.uk
letter.body:
Dear Data Protection Officer,

I am writing to raise concerns about cookie and tracking activity observed on https://www.independent.co.uk during an automated, passive audit on 2026-11-08 03:24 UTC. The audit used a fresh browser session, attempted to locate a cookie banner, and recorded what was sent before any consent choice could be made. In this case, no cookie banner or reject option was found.

The points I would like you to explain are:

1. Our review suggests that advertising trackers ran before consent was obtained. Requests to Amazon, Google, LiveRamp, Permutive and Taboola occurred before the user had answered any cookie banner, and no banner or reject option was found. The evidence identifies these services as advertising trackers. Your privacy policy states: "If you wish to browse The Independent for free, you can choose to consent to the use of cookies and similar technologies which we will use to serve relevant personalised advertising and to improve our service (including the use of analytics)."

2. Our review suggests that session-replay tracking ran before consent. Three requests to Crazy Egg, identified in the evidence as a session-replay tracker, occurred before any consent choice, and no banner or reject option was found.

3. Chartbeat cookies were set before any choice could be made. Three tracking cookies, _cb, _cb_svref and _chartbeat2, were already set before any cookie banner was answered. _cb and _chartbeat2 held what appeared to be a unique ID.

4. Six tracking companies observed during the audit do not appear to be named in the privacy policy: Chartbeat, Crazy Egg, Dotmetrics, Google, Permutive and Taboola. I appreciate the policy may refer to some recipients only by category.

5. The value of _cb and _chartbeat2, an identifier unique to this browser, was sent to chartbeat.net in the request address before any consent choice could be made.

6. Our review suggests that analytics requests also occurred before consent. Twelve requests to Dotmetrics, identified in the evidence as an analytics tracker, occurred before the user had answered any cookie banner. Your policy describes analytics as part of the cookie-based service for which users can consent.

Please:

1. Explain each of the points above.
2. Confirm which cookies and trackers you consider strictly necessary or otherwise exempt, and why.
3. Stop any non-essential tracking without consent.
4. Reply within one month.

If this matter cannot be resolved, it may be raised with the Information Commissioner’s Office.

Yours faithfully,
Joshua Baker

The analytics evidence is also concerning, although a limited analytics exception may be arguable and cannot be assessed fully from the available request data.
